sentence: We present a 24-year-old female patient who consulted the Maxillofacial Surgery Service of the San José Hospital Complex in October 2006, referred to the Dermatology Service of the same center with a diagnosis of SMR due to increased volume of the lower lip that has not shown response to treatment with intralesional and oral corticosteroids.
The patient reports that this increase in volume in the lower lip dates back to 2004, which was biopsied the same year and was histopathologically diagnosed as a KG associated with an SMR.
The initial treatment consisted of intralesional infiltrations performed in the dermatology service with betamethasone 4 mg and prednisone 0.5 mg without positive results.
In her anamnesis, she reports a morbid history of epilepsy under treatment, mild mental retardation, hypothyroidism, insulin resistance, and iodine allergy.
The drugs she regularly uses are Levothyroxine 100 mg 1 tablet / day, Carbamazepine 200 mg 1.5 tablets / day, Metformin 850 mg 1 tablet / day.

In her physical examination, a large increase in volume of the lower lip was observed, which is everted, associated with a depapillated tongue and the presence of transverse grooves on the lingual dorsum compatible with a cleft tongue as well as a discrete macroglossia.

The treatment consisted of 3 intralesional infiltrations in the lower lip of 1 ml of Kenacort®-A 40 mg (Triamcinolone acetonide) diluted in 1 ml of 2% lidocaine with the objective of controlling post-infiltration pain, with one-week intervals.

The patient was monitored for three months where a marked reduction in the size of the lower lip was evident but without yet achieving an aesthetic size, therefore a fourth infiltration was performed without any improvements being observed.
Then, a lower lip reduction cheiloplasty was scheduled under general anesthesia to improve the patient's lip aesthetics, with good results that were monitored one month postoperatively.
